metadata.title: How to Use Claude

beats.narration_text: Hallo. This is Liam, in for Bear. If you have never used an AI chat tool, start here. Most advice says: write a better prompt. But the better question is the one on screen.

show.event: backspaces 'one prompt' -> 'context' on the spoken correction

props.text:
What is the one prompt
that makes Claude work

beats.motion_claim: The writer types the naive prompt question and corrects it to the film's thesis: context.

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant-writer bookend: the correction is the motion.

beats.narration_text: Three terms. A prompt: what you type into the chat. Context: everything Claude can see about your work — your project, your constraints, your examples. And a model: the AI program behind the chat, trained to answer questions well.

beats.narration_text: Start with what you see. Claude is a chat window in your browser. You type at the bottom; the answer appears above — as simple as texting a friend.

beats.narration_text: Behind that window sits a model — an AI program trained on a huge library of writing, so it can answer questions well. The window is how you talk to it. The model is what answers.

beats.narration_text: Most people use it like a search engine. One question, one answer, close the tab. But Claude knows nothing about your project, your constraints, or what you already tried. So it answers a stranger — and the answer is generic.

beats.narration_text: Here is the one idea. Claude's answer is only as good as what it can see. Give it your project, your constraints, and an example of what good looks like — and its first draft lands close to your last draft. More context, fewer revision rounds.

shot.visual_intent: Three context cards (project, constraints, example) drop into the window one by one. The reply card grows from thin to full. Labels 'context' and 'answer'.

beats.narration_text: Projects fix this. In Claude, open a Project for the thing you are working on — a report, a garden plan, a job application. Drop in your style, your constraints, and an example you like. Do it once: every chat inside that Project starts already knowing.

shot.visual_intent: An open project box; three cards labelled style, rules, example drop in. A message rides through and an informed reply comes out. Label 'project' beside the box.

beats.narration_text: First strength: artifacts. When the answer should be a finished piece — a document, a chart, a small program — Claude builds it in a panel beside the chat. Not text to copy. A thing you can use.

beats.narration_text: Second: analysis. Hand it something long — a report, a contract, a pile of notes — and it maps the structure first, before you say what to change. Your questions get sharper, because you can see the shape of the thing.

beats.narration_text: Third: rewriting. Give it your rough draft and one example of the voice you want. It hits the tone on the first pass — and you spend your time on ideas, not phrasing.

beats.narration_text: One warning. When Claude does not know something, it can still answer confidently. So treat important facts like a first draft: check them against a source you trust.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: I'm starting [describe your project in one sentence]. My main constraint is [constraint]. What is the first question you need answered before you can actually help me? Then check two things yourself. One: does its question point at something you haven't told it yet? Answer it — that is the context it wanted. Two: does its next answer fit your constraint? If not, say so.
